title: The turfclub realm
subtitle: One Keycloak 26 realm for fourteen services, a chatbot and eleven test users
summary: Everything signs in against one realm, turfclub, imported from keycloak/turfclub-realm.json. It defines one public client for people, one confidential client per service, realm roles per module, two protocol mappers that shape every token, and the test users used throughout the videos.

sections.title: Why one realm
paragraphs: A single realm gives single sign-on across all module UIs: sign in to Core, open Horse Registry from the Modules menu and you are already signed in. Roles are realm roles, so one token describes everything a user may do in every module.
The alternative (a client role set per service) would make the token larger and the UI checks module-specific. Realm roles named <MODULE>_VIEW / <MODULE>_MANAGE keep the convention obvious.

sections.title: Clients
rows: Service-to-service calls and the outbox relay; roles SVC_READ and SVC_GL_POST
SVC_READ only: the GL receives events, it never posts them

sections.title: Protocol mappers on every client
rows: Adds a flat roles array claim (multivalued) to the ID token, access token and userinfo, with composite roles already expanded
Adds turfclub-api to the access token's aud; every resource server requires it

sections.title: Realm settings that matter
rows: Short-lived access tokens; service tokens are cached and refreshed by Spring Security
Thirty minutes of inactivity ends the SSO session
Ten hours: a full race day
Locks accounts after repeated failed sign-ins
HTTP allowed on localhost for the lab, HTTPS required from other addresses
Exactly the UIs that may receive an authorization code
Keycloak rejects any login from this client that does not send a PKCE challenge

sections.title: Import and start (lab)
sections.code:
cd keycloak-26.8.1
# one-off: import the realm (strategy IGNORE_EXISTING - delete the realm first to re-import)
bin/kc.sh import --file ~/Development/Turf_Club/turfclub-erp/keycloak/turfclub-realm.json
# every day
KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME=binitadmin KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=password bin/kc.sh start-dev --http-port=8080
